name: Question 15
problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=0,$ calculate $\text{Var}[2-\sqrt{10}X].$ 

| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.5$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ |
worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX+b]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-\sqrt{10}$ and $b=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2-\sqrt{10}X] & ={(-\sqrt{10})}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =10\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=0.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+{0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2) \\  & =1\cdot 0.5+0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.3+4\cdot 0.1 \\  & =1.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =1.2-{0}^{2} \\  & =1.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[2-\sqrt{10}X] & =10\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =10\cdot 1.2 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that for any random variable X and constants a and b, we have

Var[aX+b]=a2⋅Var[X].

In our case, a=−10 and b=2. Therefore,

Var[2−10X]=(−10)2⋅Var[X]=10⋅Var[X].

We can compute the variance of X using the following formula:

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2

Additionally, we're given that E[X]=0.

We start by computing E[X2]. Summing up the products of each value of X2 and its associated probability, we get

E[X2]=(−1)2⋅f(−1)+02⋅f(0)+12⋅f(1)+22⋅f(2)=1⋅0.5+0⋅0.1+1⋅0.3+4⋅0.1=1.2.

Therefore,

Var[X]=E[X2]−E[X]2=1.2−02=1.2.

Finally,

Var[2−10X]=10⋅Var[X]=10⋅1.2=12.
